narration: Hakken: The Dutch Heel-Stomping Rave Dance

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Hakken emerged in the early 1990s in the Netherlands, especially around The Hague and Rotterdam, within the hardcore and gabber rave scenes.
Its movements trace back to football fans at Feyenoord stadium who danced with repetitive heel stomps resembling horse mounting.
The term 'hakken' comes from the Dutch verb for chopping or striking with the heel and was popularized by rave culture expressions like 'Ik ga Hakke' ('I'm going to dance at The Hague').
on_screen: Map: Netherlands · Europe

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Hakken is a social dance within rave culture, expressing energy and connection to the hardcore music scene.
It is performed at raves, clubs, and festivals, serving as a physical embodiment of the music’s intensity and community spirit.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance consists of rapid, small steps landing primarily on the heel, following the bass drum rhythm closely.
The lower body, from the pelvis down, drives the movement, while arms and torso may move but are less emphasized.
The tempo is fast, often between 170 and 190 BPM.
Watch for Heel Tap, Backstep.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (FUD-HExh9ow)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Danced solo or in informal groups without strict spatial patterns.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Hakken is danced to hakmuziek, a genre within hardcore and gabber music characterized by a strong, steady bass drum beat around 170-190 BPM.
Contemporary hakken dancers also dance to related hard dance genres such as hardstyle, rawstyle, uptempo hardcore, and frenchcore.
Listen for the Electronic kick drum, Synthesizers, Bass lines.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 170 beats a minute.
A relentless electronic beat with a pounding bass drum at a fast tempo, layered with synthesized melodies and occasional vocal samples, creating a driving and hypnotic soundscape.
